question_english: The concept of human rights is fundamentally rooted in the belief that rights are inherent to all human beings. Which of the following is considered the defining characteristic of human rights?

The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged violation.
The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after the expiry of three years from the date of the alleged violation.
There is no time limitation; human rights violations can be inquired into at any time.
explanation_english: The correct answer is that the NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged violation. Section 36(2) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 imposes a strict statutory limitation period on the Commission’s jurisdiction. This means that if a complaint is submitted after one year from the date of the incident, the NHRC is legally barred from taking any action on it.

key_facts: Section 36(2) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 imposes a one-year limitation.
Printed answer key: (b) The NHRC cannot inquire into a matter after the expiry of one year from the date of the alleged violation.

question_english: If a human rights violation is already being inquired into by the National Human Rights Commission, what is the SHRC’s role in the same matter?
